- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast periods (e.g., first 5–10 days of 30d forecast), especially when recent history shows strong upward momentum.
- Overestimates prices after sharp spikes in recent history (e.g., after 80+ values), often overshooting by 5–10% and failing to account for subsequent mean reversion.
- Tends to ignore or underweight the influence of the most recent 5–7 days of history when forecasting, leading to lagged or delayed reactions to price reversals.
- Shows persistent downward bias in forecasts when true outcomes are trending upward, particularly in the middle-to-late portion of the 30d window.
- Overreacts to minor price fluctuations in the 30d history, especially when the last 3–5 days show volatility — leading to erratic, non-smooth forecasts.
- Underestimates the impact of policy or market events that occur within the 30d window, particularly if they are not reflected in the history data.
- Fails to adjust for seasonality or calendar effects (e.g., end-of-quarter, regulatory deadlines) unless explicitly modeled — leading to persistent bias in certain months or weeks.
- Forecasts often exhibit “sticky” behavior — once a price drops below 70, it tends to stay low for several days, even if true price rebounds — suggesting insufficient momentum capture.
